questions.title: Weekday Number and Name
questions.description:
A scheduling drill builds one calendar date from its parts and reports the weekday two ways: as the weekday() number (Monday is 0) and as the English weekday name.

Input Format:
One line: three space-separated integers y m d forming a valid calendar date.

Output Format:
Line 1: the weekday number, where Monday is 0 and Sunday is 6
Line 2: the weekday name in English

Constraints:
1900 <= y <= 2100; 1 <= m <= 12; 1 <= d <= number of days in that month.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import date

y, m, d = map(int, input().split())
dt = date(y, m, d)
print(dt.weekday())
print(dt.strftime("%A"))

questions.title: Datetime Parts Breakdown
questions.description:
A console clock drill receives five integers, constructs a datetime object explicitly, and prints each stored component on its own line.

Input Format:
One line: five space-separated integers y m d h min.

Output Format:
Five lines, exactly:
Year: <y>
Month: <m>
Day: <d>
Hour: <h>
Minute: <min>

Constraints:
2000 <= y <= 2100; 1 <= m <= 12; 1 <= d <= days in month; 0 <= h <= 23; 0 <= min <= 59.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime

y, m, d, hh, mm = map(int, input().split())
dt = datetime(y, m, d, hh, mm)
print(f"Year: {dt.year}")
print(f"Month: {dt.month}")
print(f"Day: {dt.day}")
print(f"Hour: {dt.hour}")
print(f"Minute: {dt.minute}")

questions.title: Slash Date Format Drill
questions.description:
A report formatter renders one calendar date in two notations. Given y m d, build the date and print it with strftime using the %d-%m-%Y and %Y/%m/%d codes.

Input Format:
One line: three space-separated integers y m d.

Output Format:
Line 1: the date as DD-MM-YYYY (zero-padded)
Line 2: the date as YYYY/MM/DD (zero-padded)

Constraints:
1900 <= y <= 2100; 1 <= m <= 12; 1 <= d <= days in month.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import date

y, m, d = map(int, input().split())
dt = date(y, m, d)
print(dt.strftime("%d-%m-%Y"))
print(dt.strftime("%Y/%m/%d"))

questions.title: Twelve Hour Clock Drill
questions.description:
A wall-clock drill prints one moment twice: in 24-hour notation and in 12-hour notation with an AM/PM marker. Note that 12-hour %I zero-pads and midnight prints as 12:xx AM.

Input Format:
One line: five space-separated integers y m d h min.

Output Format:
Line 1: HH:MM in 24-hour form
Line 2: hh:MM AM or hh:MM PM in 12-hour form (zero-padded hour)

Constraints:
2000 <= y <= 2100; 1 <= m <= 12; 1 <= d <= days in month; 0 <= h <= 23; 0 <= min <= 59.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime

y, mo, d, h, mi = map(int, input().split())
dt = datetime(y, mo, d, h, mi)
print(dt.strftime("%H:%M"))
print(dt.strftime("%I:%M %p"))

questions.title: Parse Then Weekday
questions.description:
A parsing drill takes a date written as DD-MM-YYYY text, converts it with strptime using the exactly matching format string, and reports the ISO form plus the weekday name.

Input Format:
One line: a date written exactly as DD-MM-YYYY (zero-padded).

Output Format:
Line 1: the same date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD form
Line 2: the weekday name in English

Constraints:
The date is a valid calendar date between 1900-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.inputconstrains: valid date between 1900-01-01 and 2100-12-31, DD-MM-YYYY zero-padded
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime

s = input()
dt = datetime.strptime(s, "%d-%m-%Y")
print(dt.date())
print(dt.strftime("%A"))

questions.title: Shift Date Forward
questions.description:
A delivery planner adds n calendar days to a start date using timedelta and prints the resulting date.

Input Format:
Line 1: a date written as DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: an integer n, the number of days to add

Output Format:
One line: the resulting date as DD-MM-YYYY

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 400; the base date is a valid calendar date between 1900-01-01 and 2100-12-31 and the result stays in the same range.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

s = input()
n = int(input())
dt = datetime.strptime(s, "%d-%m-%Y") + timedelta(days=n)
print(dt.strftime("%d-%m-%Y"))

questions.title: Flight Arrival Estimator
questions.description:
A regional airline desk estimates landing times. Given a departure timestamp and a flight duration in whole hours, the arrival moment is computed with timedelta and printed.

Input Format:
Line 1: departure timestamp as DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM (zero-padded)
Line 2: an integer, the flight duration in hours

Output Format:
One line: Arrival: DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM

Constraints:
1 <= hours <= 72; timestamps between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

dep = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
hours = int(input())
arr = dep + timedelta(hours=hours)
print(f"Arrival: {arr.strftime('%d-%m-%Y %H:%M')}")

questions.title: Prescription Refill Planner
questions.description:
A pharmacy planner schedules medicine refills. Starting from the first fill date, a refill happens every interval days; the first refill is start plus interval days, the second start plus twice the interval, and so on. Print the next three refill dates.

Input Format:
Line 1: the first fill date as DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: an integer interval in days

Output Format:
Three lines:
Refill 1: DD-MM-YYYY
Refill 2: DD-MM-YYYY
Refill 3: DD-MM-YYYY
where Refill k is start plus interval times k days.

Constraints:
1 <= interval <= 90; the start date is valid between 2000-01-01 and 2090-12-31.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

start = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
gap = int(input())
for k in range(1, 4):
    d = start + timedelta(days=gap * k)
    print(f"Refill {k}: {d.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')}")

questions.title: Library Due Date Desk
questions.description:
A library loans books for exactly 14 days. Given the issue date and the actual return date, print the due date and how many days late the book was; a return on or before the due date is 0 days overdue.

Input Format:
Line 1: issue date as DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: return date as DD-MM-YYYY

Output Format:
Line 1: Due: DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: Overdue: <n> days

Constraints:
The return date is on or after the issue date; both dates are valid between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.inputconstrains: return date >= issue date, dates between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

issue = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
ret = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
due = issue + timedelta(days=14)
late = (ret - due).days
if late < 0:
    late = 0
print(f"Due: {due.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')}")
print(f"Overdue: {late} days")

questions.title: Business Days Between Dates
questions.description:
An HR desk counts working days between two dates, inclusive of both endpoints. Saturday and Sunday are non-working days.

Input Format:
Line 1: start date as DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: end date as DD-MM-YYYY (not earlier than the start)

Output Format:
One line: the number of Monday-Friday days from start to end inclusive.

Constraints:
The range spans at most 60 days; both dates are valid calendar dates between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.inputconstrains: range spans at most 60 days, dates between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

a = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y").date()
b = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y").date()
count = 0
cur = a
while cur <= b:
    if cur.weekday() < 5:
        count += 1
    cur = cur + timedelta(days=1)
print(count)

questions.title: Age In Days Engine
questions.description:
A government form service converts a birth date into an exact age measured against a reference date, reporting the total day count and its breakdown into full weeks and leftover days using timedelta arithmetic.

Input Format:
Line 1: birth date as DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: reference date as DD-MM-YYYY (same day or later)

Output Format:
Line 1: Days: <total days between the two dates>
Line 2: Weeks: <total // 7>, Days: <total % 7>

Constraints:
Both dates are valid calendar dates between 1900-01-01 and 2100-12-31; the total is at most 73000 days.
questions.inputconstrains: reference date >= birth date, total <= 73000 days
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

birth = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
ref = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
span = ref - birth
total = span.days
print(f"Days: {total}")
rest = span - timedelta(weeks=total // 7)
print(f"Weeks: {total // 7}, Days: {rest.days}")

questions.title: Appointment Slot Conflict Check
questions.description:
A clinic scheduler stores two appointment slots written as full timestamps. Decide whether the slots overlap: they clash when slot 1 starts before slot 2 ends AND slot 2 starts before slot 1 ends. Slots that merely touch at an endpoint do not overlap.

Input Format:
Four lines, each DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM: slot 1 start, slot 1 end, slot 2 start, slot 2 end (all four share one date; each slot's end is after its start).

Output Format:
One line: Overlap or No overlap

Constraints:
All four timestamps share one date between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31; times are zero-padded HH:MM.
questions.inputconstrains: four timestamps share one date, each slot end after its start
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime

s1 = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
e1 = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
s2 = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
e2 = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
if s1 < e2 and s2 < e1:
    print("Overlap")
else:
    print("No overlap")

questions.title: Regional Date Formatter
questions.description:
A travel portal shows one ISO date in three regional styles. Parse the ISO text with strptime and produce each rendering with strftime format codes.

Input Format:
One line: a date as YYYY-MM-DD.

Output Format:
Line 1: US: MM/DD/YYYY
Line 2: EU: DD.MM.YYYY
Line 3: Long: DD Month YYYY (full English month name)

Constraints:
The date is a valid calendar date between 1900-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime

dt = datetime.strptime(input(), "%Y-%m-%d")
print(f"US: {dt.strftime('%m/%d/%Y')}")
print(f"EU: {dt.strftime('%d.%m.%Y')}")
print(f"Long: {dt.strftime('%d %B %Y')}")

questions.title: Project Milestone Ladder
questions.description:
A delivery team plans weekly milestones. Milestone i (counting from 1) happens exactly i weeks after the kickoff date. Print each milestone date in order.

Input Format:
Line 1: kickoff date as DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: an integer k, the number of milestones

Output Format:
k lines: Milestone <i>: DD-MM-YYYY for i = 1 to k.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 8; the kickoff date is valid between 2000-01-01 and 2090-12-31.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

start = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
k = int(input())
for i in range(1, k + 1):
    d = start + timedelta(weeks=i)
    print(f"Milestone {i}: {d.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')}")

questions.title: Time Of Day Classifier
questions.description:
A support desk labels incoming tickets by the time of day. Parse the 24-hour clock time with strptime and print its bucket: Morning covers 05:00-11:59, Afternoon 12:00-16:59, Evening 17:00-20:59, and Night everything else (21:00-04:59).

Input Format:
One line: a time as HH:MM (zero-padded, 24-hour).

Output Format:
One line: Morning, Afternoon, Evening, or Night

Constraints:
00 <= HH <= 23; 00 <= MM <= 59.

questions.title: Timestamp Gap Report
questions.description:
An operations dashboard reports the gap between two audit timestamps as a raw minute count and as an hours:minutes duration where hours may exceed 24.

Input Format:
Line 1: start timestamp as DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM
Line 2: end timestamp as DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM (same moment or later)

Output Format:
Line 1: Minutes: <total whole minutes>
Line 2: Duration: <H>:<MM> where H is total minutes // 60 (unpadded, may exceed 24) and MM is total minutes % 60 zero-padded

Constraints:
Both timestamps are valid between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31; the gap is at most 400 days.
questions.inputconstrains: end >= start, gap at most 400 days
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

s = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
e = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
mins = (e - s) // timedelta(minutes=1)
print(f"Minutes: {mins}")
print(f"Duration: {mins // 60}:{mins % 60:02d}")

questions.title: Multi Leg Trip Planner
questions.description:
A freight itinerary chains legs back to back: each leg departs the moment the previous leg arrives. Given the first departure timestamp and the duration in minutes of each leg, print the arrival moment of every leg in the style 01 Jan 2025 02:45.

Input Format:
Line 1: an integer k, the number of legs
Line 2: the first departure as DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM
Lines 3 to k+2: one integer per line, the duration of leg i in minutes

Output Format:
k lines: Leg <i>: DD MMM YYYY HH:MM (three-letter English month abbreviation, zero-padded day, hour and minute) for i = 1 to k.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 8; 30 <= duration <= 2000; the whole itinerary stays between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

def main():
    k = int(input())
    cur = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        minutes = int(input())
        cur = cur + timedelta(minutes=minutes)
        print(f"Leg {i}: {cur.strftime('%d %b %Y %H:%M')}")

main()

questions.title: Payroll Cutoff Engine
questions.description:
A payroll system cuts salaries on the 10th and the 25th of each month. For a given month, report both cutoff dates with a weekend flag, then count the weekend days (Saturdays and Sundays) and the working days in the whole month.

Input Format:
One line: MM-YYYY (zero-padded month, four-digit year).

Output Format:
Line 1: Cutoff 1: DD-MM-YYYY Weekend or Cutoff 1: DD-MM-YYYY Working day
Line 2: the same for Cutoff 2 (the 25th)
Line 3: Weekend days: <count of Saturdays and Sundays in the month>
Line 4: Working days: <remaining days of the month>

Constraints:
2000 <= year <= 2100; 1 <= month <= 12.
questions.sampleoutput1:
Cutoff 1: 10-05-2024 Working day
Cutoff 2: 25-05-2024 Weekend
Weekend days: 8
Working days: 23
questions.sampleoutput2:
Cutoff 1: 10-02-2024 Weekend
Cutoff 2: 25-02-2024 Weekend
Weekend days: 8
Working days: 21
questions.output1:
Cutoff 1: 10-01-2025 Working day
Cutoff 2: 25-01-2025 Weekend
Weekend days: 8
Working days: 23
questions.output2:
Cutoff 1: 10-11-2024 Weekend
Cutoff 2: 25-11-2024 Working day
Weekend days: 9
Working days: 21
questions.output3:
Cutoff 1: 10-03-2025 Working day
Cutoff 2: 25-03-2025 Working day
Weekend days: 10
Working days: 21
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime
import calendar

def main():
    first = datetime.strptime(input(), "%m-%Y")
    y, m = first.year, first.month
    ndays = calendar.monthrange(y, m)[1]
    c1 = datetime(y, m, 10)
    c2 = datetime(y, m, 25)
    flag1 = "Weekend" if c1.weekday() >= 5 else "Working day"
    flag2 = "Weekend" if c2.weekday() >= 5 else "Working day"
    wknd = 0
    for dnum in range(1, ndays + 1):
        if datetime(y, m, dnum).weekday() >= 5:
            wknd += 1
    print(f"Cutoff 1: {c1.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')} {flag1}")
    print(f"Cutoff 2: {c2.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')} {flag2}")
    print(f"Weekend days: {wknd}")
    print(f"Working days: {ndays - wknd}")

main()

questions.title: Medicine Dose Schedule Matrix
questions.description:
A hospital infusion planner prints a dose card. Doses are taken every H hours; dose i (counting from 1) falls at start plus i times H hours. Print each dose in 12-hour notation and count how many doses fall in the night window (24-hour hour of 20 or later, or before 06:00).

Input Format:
Line 1: the first dose timestamp as DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM
Line 2: two space-separated integers H (interval hours) and k (number of doses)

Output Format:
k lines: Dose <i>: DD-MM-YYYY hh:MM AM or PM (12-hour zero-padded clock)
Final line: Night doses: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= H <= 24; 1 <= k <= 6; timestamps valid between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

def main():
    start = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
    h, k = map(int, input().split())
    night = 0
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        t = start + timedelta(hours=h * i)
        if t.hour >= 20 or t.hour < 6:
            night += 1
        print(f"Dose {i}: {t.strftime('%d-%m-%Y %I:%M %p')}")
    print(f"Night doses: {night}")

main()

questions.title: Date Range Audit Trail
questions.description:
An auditor walks a date range day by day. For every date from start to end inclusive, print the date with its weekday name, tagging the last day of each month. Finish with the number of month-end days encountered.

Input Format:
Line 1: start date as DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: end date as DD-MM-YYYY (not earlier than the start)

Output Format:
One line per date: DD-MM-YYYY <WeekdayName> and, when the date is the last day of its month, append  [Month end] (a space before the bracket)
Final line: Month ends: <count>

Constraints:
The range spans at most 40 days (1 <= end - start + 1 <= 40); both dates are valid calendar dates between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.sampleoutput1:
28-02-2024 Wednesday
29-02-2024 Thursday [Month end]
01-03-2024 Friday
02-03-2024 Saturday
Month ends: 1
questions.sampleoutput2:
29-12-2023 Friday
30-12-2023 Saturday
31-12-2023 Sunday [Month end]
01-01-2024 Monday
02-01-2024 Tuesday
Month ends: 1
questions.output3:
27-02-2025 Thursday
28-02-2025 Friday [Month end]
01-03-2025 Saturday
Month ends: 1
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= range span <= 40 days, dates between 2000-01-01 and 2100-12-31
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

NAMES = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]

def main():
    a = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
    b = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
    ends = 0
    cur = a
    while cur <= b:
        nxt = cur + timedelta(days=1)
        mark = ""
        if nxt.day == 1:
            mark = " [Month end]"
            ends += 1
        print(f"{cur.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')} {NAMES[cur.weekday()]}{mark}")
        cur = nxt
    print(f"Month ends: {ends}")

main()
